description: Rewire frontend/src/components/Collections.tsx so the driver assignment/release/availability/workflow flows call the REAL backend endpoints (added in FEAT-001 plus existing ones) instead of the non-existent collection-ops/* and collections-state-sync/auto-assign|release|workflow routes. Also remove the throwing/unreachable/dead-fallback code paths so a courier's first use does not hit runtime failures. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: fetchDrivers(): replace the try GET /drivers/available -> catch GET /collection-ops/driver-availability chain with a single call to api.get('/drivers', { params: { status: 'AVAILABLE' } }). Keep the existing extractDrivers(res.data) normalization and the outer try/catch that sets drivers to [] on failure. (GET /drivers exists and supports the status filter.)

autoAssignDriver(collectionId): this function currently POSTs to /collections-state-sync/auto-assign/:id which does NOT exist and has NO try/catch so it THROWS. Change it to derive the best driver from the existing suggestion endpoint then assign via the new route: call GET /collections-state-sync/suggest-driver/:id (already used elsewhere via getSuggestedDriver) to get { suggestion }, take suggestion.id (fall back to the first available driver from the drivers state if no suggestion), then POST /collections/:id/assign-driver { driverId }. Return the assignment response. Wrap in try/catch OR let the callers (assignDrawerRecommendedDriver already wraps in try/catch) handle it — keep behavior that the caller shows a toast/message. If no driver can be determined, throw a clear Error('No available driver to assign') so the existing caller catch surfaces a friendly message.

assignDriverToCollection(collectionId, driverId): replace the three-way fallback (POST /collections/:id/assign-driver -> /drivers/assign -> /collection-ops/assign-driver/:id) with a single POST /collections/:id/assign-driver { driverId } (now real). Return the axios response. Remove the dead fallbacks.

releaseDriverFromCollection(collectionId): replace the dead POST /collection-ops/release-driver/:id -> /collections-state-sync/release/:id chain (which also has UNREACHABLE code after the return) with a single POST /collections/:id/release-driver (now real). Remove the unreachable requestLiveRefresh() line; if a refresh is desired keep exactly one requestLiveRefresh() call BEFORE the return or let the caller (releaseDrawerDriver) handle refresh as it already does.

openLinkedWorkflow(record): the Promise.all currently calls api.get('/collections-state-sync/workflow/:id') which does NOT exist. Change that call to api.get('/collections/:collectionKey/workflow') (the new GET route from FEAT-001). Keep the getSuggestedDriver(collectionKey) call unchanged (that endpoint exists). The rest of the resolve/drawer logic already tolerates the returned shape via resolveCollectionTruth.

Do a final read-through of Collections.tsx to confirm there are no remaining references to '/collection-ops/', '/drivers/available', '/drivers/assign', '/collections-state-sync/auto-assign', '/collections-state-sync/release', or '/collections-state-sync/workflow'. Confirm no unreachable statements remain (no code after a return within the same block).
Do NOT change the working endpoints already in the file: /collections-state-sync/dashboard, /records, /bulk-sync, /sync/:id, /suggest-driver/:id — these exist and are correct.
acceptance_criteria: grep of Collections.tsx returns ZERO matches for '/collection-ops/', '/drivers/available', '/drivers/assign', 'collections-state-sync/auto-assign', 'collections-state-sync/release', and 'collections-state-sync/workflow'.
fetchDrivers calls GET /drivers with params { status: 'AVAILABLE' }.
assignDriverToCollection calls exactly POST /collections/:id/assign-driver with { driverId } and no fallbacks.
releaseDriverFromCollection calls exactly POST /collections/:id/release-driver and contains no unreachable code after a return.

autoAssignDriver no longer calls a non-existent route and cannot throw an unhandled error for the normal 'no suggestion' case (it either assigns a real driver or throws a descriptive Error caught by its caller).
verification: Run `grep -nE "collection-ops|drivers/available|drivers/assign|auto-assign|collections-state-sync/(release|workflow)" frontend/src/components/Collections.tsx` and confirm no matches.

Read the five changed functions and confirm each targets a route that exists after FEAT-001 (assign-driver, release-driver, workflow on /collections; /drivers?status; /collections-state-sync/suggest-driver).
Confirm no unreachable statements remain in releaseDriverFromCollection (the requestLiveRefresh after return is removed).
findings: Edited only frontend/src/components/Collections.tsx. (1) fetchDrivers now does a single api.get('/drivers', { params: { status: 'AVAILABLE' } }), kept extractDrivers normalization and outer try/catch -> setDrivers([]). (2) autoAssignDriver now calls getSuggestedDriver (GET /collections-state-sync/suggest-driver/:id), takes suggestion.id, falls back to drivers[0]?.id, throws Error('No available driver to assign') if none, then POST /collections/:id/assign-driver { driverId }; removed the dead /collections-state-sync/auto-assign POST and the errant requestLiveRefresh. (3) assignDriverToCollection reduced to single POST /collections/:id/assign-driver { driverId }, fallbacks removed. (4) releaseDriverFromCollection reduced to single POST /collections/:id/release-driver; unreachable requestLiveRefresh after return removed (caller releaseDrawerDriver already refreshes). (5) openLinkedWorkflow now GETs /collections/:id/workflow (getSuggestedDriver call left unchanged). Left working routes untouched: /collections-state-sync/dashboard, /records, /bulk-sync, /sync/:id, /suggest-driver/:id. Verified via grep: ZERO matches for collection-ops, drivers/available, drivers/assign, collections-state-sync/auto-assign, collections-state-sync/release, collections-state-sync/workflow. Driver.id is typed string, so drivers[0]?.id and suggestion?.id resolve to string|undefined and are TS-consistent. No build/test run: no node/npm in sandbox (static verification only, per context.json).
